requirement: Students analyze a read-aloud passage to extract the main idea or central message through systematic text evidence collection. Focus: Determining the overall point or central message of the narrative or text. Examples: The importance of kindness, the lesson learned by the protagonist, the significance of the invention, the moral of the fable, the primary topic of the report, why the animal adapted to its habitat, how weather affects the local ecosystem, the reason for the city festival. Constraints: The passage-studio must provide a short text segment where the student chooses the one best sentence that summarizes the entire passage from a list of distractors.

fullData.title: Uncovering the Big Story Message
fullData.description: A 4-part narrated walkthrough with a check after each part.

segments.title: Searching for the Big Idea
segments.script: Every story has a central message, which is the main lesson or big idea the author wants us to learn. We can act like detectives by collecting clues called text evidence as we listen carefully. When we connect those clues together, they reveal the author's overall point!
segments.imagePrompt: A friendly young girl and boy wearing detective hats in a cozy classroom reading nook, holding colorful magnifying glasses over an open storybook with glowing golden clue symbols floating upward, warm storybook illustration style, bright cheerful colors.

knowledgeCheck.question: What clues do readers collect from sentences to find the central message?
options: Guesses about how the book ends
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The script explains that readers act like detectives by collecting clues called text evidence to find the central message.

segments.title: Pip's Helpful Choice
segments.script: Listen to this short passage: Pip the squirrel collected a giant pile of acorns, but his neighbor Ollie had a hurt paw and could not search for food. Pip noticed Ollie looking hungry and sad, so Pip carried half of his own acorns over to Ollie's hollow tree. Ollie smiled with relief, and Pip felt a warm joy in his heart.
segments.imagePrompt: A cute fluffy squirrel named Pip gently placing golden acorns in front of another squirrel with a bandaged paw outside a cozy hollow tree nest, autumnal forest background with falling leaves, warm and friendly children's picture book art style.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why did Pip carry his acorns over to Ollie's tree?
options: A heavy rainstorm washed the acorns away
Pip wanted to trade his acorns for sweet berries
Ollie had a hurt paw and could not search for food
Pip had too many acorns to keep in his nest
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The passage states that Ollie had a hurt paw and could not search for food, which is why Pip decided to help him.

segments.title: Gathering Text Evidence
segments.script: Let us review our evidence: Ollie was in trouble, Pip gave away his food, and both squirrels ended up happy. Acorns and trees are just tiny details, but helping a friend is the big idea that ties them all together. A true central message must explain the whole story rather than just one small part.
segments.imagePrompt: A three-step evidence board in a sunny classroom showing drawn cards of Ollie needing help, Pip sharing his acorns, and both squirrels smiling together under an umbrella labeled Central Message, clean 2D vector educational art.

knowledgeCheck.question: According to the script, what must a true central message do?
options: Change the ending to make it surprising
Explain the whole story rather than just one small part
Name every single tree in the forest
Focus only on one tiny detail like acorns
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The script teaches that a true central message must explain the whole story rather than focusing on just one small detail.

segments.title: Finding the Best Summary
segments.script: Now we test our sentences to find the one best summary for the whole passage. Sentences like 'Acorns are crunchy' or 'Ollie hurt his paw' only tell tiny facts from one moment. The sentence that truly summarizes the entire passage is: Kind actions and sharing bring happiness to everyone.
segments.imagePrompt: A friendly animal teacher pointing to a chalkboard with three sentences crossed out and one glowing sentence highlighted in bright yellow that says sharing brings joy, whimsical elementary school classroom setting, gentle pastel tones.

knowledgeCheck.question: Which sentence best summarizes the entire passage about Pip and Ollie?
options: Ollie hurt his paw in the woods.
Squirrels make homes inside hollow forest trees.
Kind actions and sharing bring happiness to everyone.
knowledgeCheck.explanation: The script identifies 'Kind actions and sharing bring happiness to everyone' as the sentence that summarizes the entire story rather than just a small detail.
